adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These expressions evaluate at runtime to a single constant property name (stringified Zod objects, effectively `"[object Object]"`), so they do not create a wildcard/record schema for “any numeric expiry field” or “any other fields”. Since `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default (no `.passthrough()`), in credential-sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the parse result will drop fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in` and any other token fields, leaving only `access_token`. The helper then injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever it’s missing, which can overwrite/propagate a literal placeholder refresh token via call sites that merge/persist `tokenResponse.data` (e.g., Office365 merges `tokenResponse.data` into stored credentials; Zoom similarly now uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse`). This is grounded in the diff and would cause incorrect/stale expiry handling and potentially corrupted stored refresh tokens.
